high.title: Minister Purbaya Plans to Aggressively Chase Tax Delinquents
high.summary: Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced the government will accelerate tax collection efforts in 2026, leveraging the Coretax software system to eliminate tax leakage and manipulation. The Directorate General of Taxation will take a more active role in pursuing outstanding tax obligations, including acting on public reports of non-compliance. This signals a more aggressive fiscal enforcement stance that could impact businesses and high-net-worth individuals with unresolved tax liabilities.

high.title: Full List of New Fuel Prices at All Gas Stations
high.summary: Pertamina and several private fuel companies have adjusted their fuel prices effective August 1, with Pertamina cutting prices on non-subsidized fuels Pertamax (RON 92), Pertamax Green 95, and Pertamax Turbo. BP and VIVO also reduced prices on select products, while Shell, BP Ultimate Diesel, and VIVO Diesel Primus saw price increases. These price adjustments have broad implications for inflation, consumer spending, and energy sector stocks in Indonesia.

high.title: JCI Strengthens 1.70% to 5,792 – Conglomerate and SOE Stocks Surge
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) gained 1.70% to close Session I at 5,792.16, with intraday highs reaching 5,806.71, driven by strong performance in conglomerate and state-owned enterprise (SOE) stocks. Transaction volume reached 13.08 billion shares valued at IDR 6.49 trillion across 925,909 trades. This broad-based rally signals renewed investor confidence and is significant for market participants tracking blue-chip and SOE sector momentum.

high.title: BPS Reports July 2026 Deflation of 0.14%; Annual Inflation at 2.88%
high.summary: Indonesia's Central Statistics Agency (BPS) recorded a monthly deflation of 0.14% in July 2026, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) falling from 111.89 to 111.73, primarily driven by a 0.89% decline in food, beverages, and tobacco prices. On an annual basis, inflation stood at 2.88% (YoY) and 1.65% year-to-date. This deflation data is a key macroeconomic indicator that may influence Bank Indonesia's monetary policy decisions and investor expectations for interest rate movements.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Rises to IDR 2,610,000 per Gram
high.summary: Antam's 24-karat gold price increased by IDR 7,000 per gram to IDR 2,610,000 on Monday (3/8/2026), with the 1-kg bar priced at IDR 2.55 billion. However, over the past week and month, prices have trended downward from a recent high of IDR 2,670,000 per gram. Gold price movements are closely watched by Indonesian investors as a safe-haven indicator and a reflection of global risk sentiment.

high.title: Bulog Receives Full Financial Support from Government for Food Self-Sufficiency
high.summary: The government has issued Bapanas Regulation No. 3 dated July 29, 2026, significantly increasing Bulog's assignment margin to 7% or approximately Rp 970 per unit, up sharply from the previous margin of only around Rp 50. This policy shift substantially strengthens Bulog's financial position as the national food operator and creates greater fiscal efficiency for the state. This is a major regulatory change impacting Indonesia's food supply chain and state-owned enterprise economics.

high.title: BPS: July 2026 Records Deflation of 0.14%
high.summary: Indonesia's Central Statistics Agency (BPS) recorded a monthly deflation of 0.14% in July 2026, with annual inflation at 2.88% and year-to-date inflation at 1.65%. The primary driver of deflation was the food, beverages, and tobacco category, which posted a deflation of 0.89%. This data is significant for investors as it signals easing price pressures and may influence Bank Indonesia's future monetary policy decisions.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Rises to Rp 2,610,000 per Gram
high.summary: Antam's 24-karat gold price increased by Rp 7,000 per gram to Rp 2,610,000 on Monday, August 3, 2026. Despite the daily gain, the price remains within a declining trend over the past week and month, with recent ranges of Rp 2,601,000–2,670,000 over the last 30 days. This is a key indicator for commodity investors and those tracking safe-haven asset movements in Indonesia.

high.title: KAI's Profit Drops Sharply in First Half of 2026
high.summary: State-owned railway company KAI reported a significant decline in net profit for H1 2026, with current year profit falling to Rp 314.03 billion from Rp 1.18 trillion in the same period last year — a drop of over 73%. Despite revenue growing 6.6% to Rp 17.96 trillion, rising costs have severely compressed margins, raising concerns about profitability sustainability for investors in the state-owned enterprise sector.

high.title: OJK Reveals Evidence of IHSG Recovery
high.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi confirmed that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,236.13 on July 31, 2026, recovering 10.51% month-to-date after hitting a low of 5,643.19 at the end of Q2 2026. The Q2 close represented a steep 19.93% quarter-on-quarter correction driven by global uncertainty and portfolio rebalancing by investors. The July recovery signals a potential bullish turning point for Indonesian capital markets.

high.title: Trump Intervenes to Help Japan Strengthen Yen Against US Dollar
high.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance conducted a coordinated yen-buying intervention with the US Treasury Department starting Friday, July 31, after the yen weakened to 163.73 per USD — its weakest level in four decades. The coordinated action pushed the yen back to 157.57 by Friday and it was trading at 157.70 on Monday. This rare US-Japan currency coordination signals heightened global forex volatility, which could impact the Indonesian Rupiah and regional emerging market currencies.

high.title: IHSG Reverses to Weaken to 6,234 in Session I
high.summary: The IHSG reversed early gains to close the first trading session down 0.03% at 6,234.29, in line with broad weakness across most Asian markets. The index had briefly touched a high of 6,273.32 in the morning session before retreating. Trading volume reached 23.09 billion shares with a transaction value of IDR 7.68 trillion in the first half of the session.

medium.title: President Prabowo Urges Business Leaders to Stay United Amid Global Economic Uncertainty
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto met with Kadin (Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry) leaders and association heads at the Presidential Palace, calling for national elite unity and compliance with laws amid volatile global economic conditions. Business leaders responded positively, pledging to maintain a positive stance toward Indonesia's economic activity. The meeting signals a government push for closer cooperation with the private sector to shore up economic confidence.

medium.title: Kadin Chief Reveals Indonesian-Made Components Used by Tesla, IKEA, and Airbus
medium.summary: Kadin Chairman Anindya Bakrie highlighted Indonesia's growing role as a key player in global supply chains, with domestic products already integrated into the ecosystems of major global companies such as Tesla, Airbus, and IKEA. The disclosure, made during a meeting with President Prabowo at the Presidential Palace, underscores Indonesia's manufacturing competitiveness and export potential. This is positive news for investors in Indonesian manufacturing and export-oriented sectors.

medium.title: CPO Reference Price Falls Due to Sluggish Global Demand
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Trade set the August 2026 reference price for crude palm oil (CPO) at US$996.52 per metric ton, a decline of US$4.38 (0.44%) from the previous month, reflecting weakening global demand. The export duty remains at US$148/MT and the export levy is set at 12.5% of the reference price, equating to US$124.56/MT. Investors in palm oil stocks and related agribusiness sectors should note the marginal price softening, which may affect export revenues for CPO producers.

medium.title: Garuda Indonesia Speaks Out on State-Owned Airline Holding Plan with Pelita Air
medium.summary: PT Garuda Indonesia (Persero) Tbk has confirmed that a consolidation plan involving Pelita Air is currently under intensive review with shareholders and relevant stakeholders. The study covers strategic direction, structure, timeline, and execution mechanisms as part of Garuda Indonesia Group's broader transformation agenda. This corporate action could significantly impact Garuda's share price and the competitive landscape of Indonesian aviation.

medium.title: KAI's Profit Drops Sharply — Here's the Main Cause
medium.summary: PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) reported a significant decline in profitability in H1 2026, with pre-tax profit falling to Rp 842.69 billion and net profit dropping to Rp 314.03 billion, compared to Rp 1.86 trillion and Rp 1.18 trillion respectively in H1 2025. The main driver of the decline was a surge in net losses from associates and joint ventures, rising from Rp 948.20 billion to Rp 3.00 trillion. Despite this, KAI's revenue grew 6.6% year-on-year to Rp 17.96 trillion, indicating operational strength undermined by investment-related losses.

medium.title: KUR Loans Under Rp 100 Million Prohibited from Requiring Collateral
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of SMEs has reaffirmed that KUR (People's Business Credit) loans up to Rp 100 million must not require any additional collateral, in line with official KUR implementation guidelines. The public is urged to report any violations, including demands for collateral, fees, or the use of brokers. This regulatory clarification aims to improve MSME access to credit and curb predatory lending practices around the government's flagship SME loan program.

medium.title: Rice Aid to Be Distributed Simultaneously on August 17th Independence Day
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Food Agency (Bapanas) has officially tasked Bulog with distributing government food reserves (CPP) as rice aid for July, August, and September 2026 to over 33.2 million recipients, each receiving 10 kg. The distribution is set to coincide with Indonesia's 81st Independence Day on August 17. This government social safety net program is designed to support purchasing power, stabilize food prices, and has direct operational significance for Bulog's logistics and rice market dynamics.

medium.title: Bank Mandiri and Telkom Conduct Aggressive Share Buybacks Amid Sluggish JCI
medium.summary: Indonesia's Deputy House Speaker Sufmi Dasco Ahmad met with the head of the SOE Supervisory Board, the State Secretary Minister, and Himbara (State-Owned Banks Association) executives to discuss capital market volatility and share buyback strategies for SOE stocks. Officials affirmed that state-owned bank fundamentals remain strong, with the recent stock price declines attributed to global market turbulence rather than domestic weaknesses. The coordinated buyback initiative signals government support for SOE share prices and may provide a floor for bank stocks during periods of global uncertainty.

medium.title: Bakrie Group's Electric Bus Issuer VKTR Posts IDR 647 Billion in Sales and IDR 10 Billion Net Profit in H1 2026
medium.summary: PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR), the Bakrie Group's electric bus subsidiary, reported net sales of IDR 647 billion in H1 2026, a 56% YoY increase, supported by growing commercial EV adoption and automotive parts manufacturing recovery. Operating profit surged 1,890% YoY to IDR 16 billion, while net profit grew 25% YoY to IDR 10 billion. The strong performance highlights the growth trajectory of Indonesia's electric vehicle sector and is relevant for investors tracking EV-related equities on the IDX.

medium.title: Root Cause of KAI's Sharply Declining Profit Revealed
medium.summary: State-owned railway company KAI recorded a steep drop in profitability in H1-2026, with pre-tax profit falling to Rp 842.69 billion and net profit to Rp 314.03 billion, compared to Rp 1.86 trillion and Rp 1.18 trillion respectively in the same period last year. Despite revenue growing 6.6% year-on-year to Rp 17.96 trillion, rising costs appear to have severely compressed margins. This is a key concern for investors monitoring state-owned enterprise (SOE) performance in Indonesia's transportation sector.

medium.title: Bulog Guarantees Free Nutritious Meal Program Does Not Use Subsidized Rice or Minyakita
medium.summary: Bulog's CEO confirmed that all food supplies provided for the government's Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program consist of premium-grade products, not subsidized SPHP rice or Minyakita cooking oil. This clarification follows the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) chief's warning about an ongoing investigation into MBG kitchens suspected of using subsidized goods. The issue has implications for subsidy distribution integrity and the operational credibility of the flagship MBG program.

medium.title: BGN Chief Threatens to Fire MBG Kitchen Staff Who Violate Standard Operating Procedures
medium.summary: The head of the National Nutrition Agency (BGN), Sudaryono, declared a zero-tolerance policy on food safety violations and corruption within the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program following a food poisoning incident affecting hundreds of students at SMK Negeri 6 Semarang. He threatened immediate dismissal of any kitchen staff failing to comply with SOPs and vowed to eliminate corrupt practices such as unofficial fee collections. This highlights growing governance and food safety risks in one of the government's flagship social programs.

medium.title: Thailand Offers to Supply Quality Rice, Seeks to Import Indonesian Fertilizer
medium.summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul proposed deeper bilateral cooperation with Indonesia in food and agriculture during a meeting with President Prabowo, offering Thailand as a reliable supplier of high-quality rice and agricultural machinery. In return, Thailand expressed interest in importing Indonesian fertilizer and expanding trade in meat and dairy products. This development is relevant to Indonesia's food security strategy and agricultural trade balance.

medium.title: Stocks Not Meeting Free Float Requirements to Receive 'P' Notation — Here Are the Details
medium.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) introduced a new special notation system effective July 31, 2026, adding Notation 'P' for listed companies that have not met free float requirements, while removing previous notations E, D, A, and S. The change is part of IDX's broader capital market reform agenda to enhance disclosure quality and investor protection. Investors should be aware of this new notation system as it directly affects how to assess the liquidity and compliance status of listed companies.

medium.title: IHSG Opens Stronger to 6,254 at the Start of the Week
medium.summary: The IHSG opened the week in positive territory, rising 18.1 points (0.29%) to 6,249 as of 09:05 WIB on Monday, August 3, 2026, with an opening at 6,272. Early morning transaction value reached IDR 1.14 trillion involving 2.99 billion shares traded 183,985 times. The positive open reflected continued recovery momentum from the prior month's strong gains.
